=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clear paired leaves at visible nodes along stem, alternating above and below)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves spaced along stem with visible internodes, not tightly clustered)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without divisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broad in middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (comes to a sharp, pointed tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is gently curved, not tapered or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, multiple pairs (secondary veins clearly visible, running parallel to each other from midrib to margin)

    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short compared to leaf blade, not elongated)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (circular in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody or lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)

    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels visible, surface appears uniform)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no structures at leaf base resembling stipules visible)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible when stem is cut or damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base visible)
